stem: An 8-month-old has cough, wheeze and crackles during a viral lower respiratory illness, with a similar episode documented 6 weeks ago; which detail most strongly argues against bronchiolitis?

options.text: The child is younger than 12 months
This is not the first episode of viral-induced lower respiratory illness
The illness affects the lower respiratory tract

explanation: Bronchiolitis is the first episode of viral-induced lower respiratory illness in an infant under 12 months, so a previous similar episode argues against this label.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because being younger than 12 months supports the bronchiolitis definition.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because bronchiolitis is defined here as the first episode of viral-induced lower respiratory illness, so a prior similar episode makes bronchiolitis less likely.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because wheeze is compatible with bronchiolitis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because crackles are also compatible with bronchiolitis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because lower respiratory tract involvement is part of the bronchiolitis presentation.
